articles.content_excerpt: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. We have a monumental math problem in America, and what is broken cannot be repaired by tinkering around the edges. The Jurassic Republicans were right about one thing: There is no free lunch. But they were mistaken in believing there is such a thing as a truly free market. Every economic transaction depends on infrastructure, education, public safety, environmental protection, and countless other necessities that markets cannot simply conjure out of thin air. Yet the prices we pay for goods and services seldom reflect their full costs to society. articles.title: The UAW Bet on Abdul El-Sayed and Won
articles.author: Alex N. Press
articles.content_excerpt: Three Rivers, Michigan, is a factory town in a county where Donald Trump won 66.2 percent of the vote in 2024. Its biggest employer is American Axle, whose workers belong to United Auto Workers (UAW) Local 2093. In 2008, the company demanded major concessions, arguing that it needed lower labor costs to remain competitive and keep the plant open. Workers spent nearly three months on strike before accepting a contract that halved some workers’ pay, from $29 an hour to $14.50. The plant survived, but by this spring, production workers still topped out at only $22 an hour. Workers spent years trying to recover what they had lost. articles.title: The Democratic Coalition Still Has a Class Problem
articles.author: Jared Abbott
articles.content_excerpt: Democrats won a massive victory in the 2026 midterms, performing so well that Republicans’ best-laid gerrymandering plans actually backfired in a number of states, most notably Texas and North Carolina . There, Democrats held most of the seats Republicans had targeted and even flipped some districts drawn to be safely Republican. Democrats flipped Senate seats in places like Texas, Kansas, and South Carolina that were considered virtually unimaginable reaches in the very recent past. That’s of course very good for the party, and, I would hasten to add, for our fight against the ever-present threat of the far right. articles.title: Elections in a Genocidal State Are Not Democratic
articles.author: Raz Segal
articles.content_excerpt: The recent Israeli elections are a grotesque spectacle. They are grotesque because Israel is a state perpetrating genocide against Palestinians in the Gaza Strip, cheered on by most of its Jewish citizens. They are grotesque because they peddle the lie of democracy in a state subjecting millions of Palestinians in the West Bank and the Gaza Strip to a brutal military occupation for nearly six decades, without basic rights, dispossessing them to settle more than 750,000 Jews in crude violation of basic international law. And they are grotesque because they promote the illusion, both within and outside Israel, that nearly two million Palestinian citizens of Israel somehow hold the key to saving the state from itself. articles.title: After the Midterms, the Left Has a Huge Opportunity to Seize
articles.author: Eric Blanc
articles.content_excerpt: This week’s midterm results were a historic victory for working people and a devastating blow to Trumpism. After so much cruelty and darkness, millions of people have gotten to experience the joy of defeating the far right. We’re entering an unusually fluid political moment, with enormous opportunities, formidable opponents, and no ready-made road map. Here are my initial thoughts about how we got here and what we should do now. 1. America Is Not a Deeply Right-Wing Country Remember when centrist pundits insisted Trump’s 2024 victory meant America had become permanently conservative? That narrative hasn’t aged well. articles.title: Can the DSA Build Working-Class Power?
articles.author: Paul Heideman
articles.content_excerpt: Over the past decade, the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) has moved from an obscure Cold War holdover to one of the most influential organizations in US politics. But even with continued electoral success, is it at risk of stalling out? As far back as high school, and I’m now 78, I’ve always been a glass-half-empty kind of guy. Looking at the world that way means that I’m almost never disappointed. And every now and then, I get to be pleasantly surprised. One of those pleasant surprises—and a very pleasant surprise it was—came with the recent US mid-term elections. Only a few weeks ago, I wrote an essay called “It’s Election Time Again” in which I warned people not to get too excited about some anticipated Big Blue Wave this time around. Seldom has a party scored such a comprehensive demolition of its opposition. Yet the prime author was not the Democrats themselves, but their dominant adversary, Donald Trump. He created the economic conditions that impelled many of those who voted for him just two years ago to repudiate him now. His tariffs raised costs to consumers. His war in Iran led to the blockage of the Persian Gulf sea lanes and the explosion of fuel prices. His public obsession with self-glorifying monument construction, even as most people had trouble making ends meet, jut reinforced the public rage. articles.content_excerpt: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. Why should you still care about AB 32, two decades after Gov. Arnold Schwarzenegger signed it into law? Not just because the “California Global Warming Solutions Act of 2006” remains in effect, and enjoys support of 75% of state residents, according to a 2026 poll by the Public Policy Institute of California. Nor because AB 32 is the foundation for California’s climate regulation regime has reduced per-capita greenhouse gas emissions by 29%. Since nearly all of the discussion of the unhoused people in the Los Angeles area focuses on the homeless, we need to consider the over-crowded . These are the people who still have a roof over the head, but are mostly confined to small apartments. They are one step away from being homeless, and they include lots of kids. The photo above demonstrates the conditions in which the overcrowed live, packing themselves and their belongings into a small space. This is not by choice, but an obvious way for over a million people to avoid living on the streets. articles.title: Political Extinction of Biblical Proportions: Democrats, Never Forgive and Forget!
articles.author: Desi Cortez
articles.content_excerpt: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. America may be approaching a political extinction of damn-near biblical proportions. Not the extinction of a people, but of a toxic political philosophy that confuses meanness with genius, force and harassment with courage, greed with gumption, and the U.S. Constitution with bathroom tissue. After the November 3 midterms handed Democrats control of Congress, I hear Washington preparing its favorite lullaby: Kumbaya, my Lord, kumbaya. Let’s heal. Let’s move on. Let’s work together.
